title: Done, doing, and ever done
title_target: 食咗飯未呀？ — Sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3?
goal: Master the Cantonese aspect markers — 咗, 緊, 過, 晒, 住 — and, most importantly, understand that 咗 is not a past tense, so it isn't negated with 唔.
bekal: mark completion with 咗 and negate it with 冇 or 未
mark an action in progress with 緊
use 晒 (all gone, all of it) and 住 (stay that way)
tell 咗 (a verb marker) apart from 喇 (a sentence-final particle)

dialogs.title: 對話 1 — An afternoon phone call
dialogs.intro: Wong Lai calls Andi. This short conversation packs in four aspect markers — read it slowly and notice where each marker sits.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [喂|Wai2]，[安迪|On1 dik1]？[你食咗飯未呀|Nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3]？
lines.id: Hello, Andi? Have you eaten yet?
lines.literal: hello, Andi. you — eat — already — rice — not-yet — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [仲未|Zung6 mei6]。[我做緊嘢|Ngo5 zou6 gan2 je5]。[你呢|Nei5 ne1]？
lines.id: Not yet. I'm working. You?
lines.literal: still — not-yet. I — do — -ing — stuff. you — how.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [我食咗喇|Ngo5 sik6 zo2 laa3]。[你做緊咩呀|Nei5 zou6 gan2 me1 aa3]？
lines.id: I have. What are you doing?
lines.literal: I — eat — already — already. you — do — -ing — what — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [改緊功課|Goi2 gan2 gung1 fo3]。[改咗一半|Goi2 zo2 jat1 bun3]，[仲有好多|zung6 jau5 hou2 do1]。
lines.id: Marking homework. Half of it's done, there's still lots left.
lines.literal: correct — -ing — home — work. correct — already — one — half, still — have — filler — much.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你琴日|Nei5 kam4 jat6][去咗邊度呀|heoi3 zo2 bin1 dou6 aa3]？[我搵你搵咗好耐|Ngo5 wan2 nei5 wan2 zo2 hou2 noi6]。
lines.id: Where did you go yesterday? I looked for you for ages.
lines.literal: you — yesterday — go — already — which — place — huh. I — look-for — you — look-for — already — filler — long.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [我冇去邊度|Ngo5 mou5 heoi3 bin1 dou6]，[我瞓咗成日|ngo5 fan3 zo2 seng4 jat6]。
lines.id: I didn't go anywhere, I slept all day.
lines.literal: I — not — go — which — place, I — sleep — already — whole — day.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你病咗咩|Nei5 beng6 zo2 me1]？
lines.id: Oh, were you sick?
lines.literal: you — sick — already — really.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [冇|Mou5]，[得閒|dak1 haan4][啫|ze1]。[我未去過長洲|Ngo5 mei6 heoi3 gwo3 Coeng4 zau1]，[你去過未呀|nei5 heoi3 gwo3 mei6 aa3]？
lines.id: No, just had free time. I've never been to Cheung Chau — have you?
lines.literal: not-have, free — just. I — not-yet — go — ever — Cheung-Chau, you — go — ever — not-yet — huh.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [去過好多次|Heoi3 gwo3 hou2 do1 ci3]！[星期六一齊去|Sing1 kei4 luk6 jat1 cai4 heoi3][好唔好|hou2 m4 hou2]？
lines.id: Lots of times! Shall we go together on Saturday?
lines.literal: go — ever — filler — many — times. week — six — together — go — good — not — good.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [好呀|Hou2 aa3]！[等我做完功課先|Dang2 ngo5 zou6 jyun4 gung1 fo3 sin1]。
lines.id: Sure! Wait till I finish the homework first.
lines.literal: good — huh. wait — I — do — finish — homework — first.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [得|Dak1]。[做完打電話畀我|Zou6 jyun4 daa2 din6 waa2 bei2 ngo5]。[記住呀|Gei3 zyu6 aa3]！
lines.id: OK. Call me when you're done. Don't forget!
lines.literal: can. do — finish — dial — phone — give — me. remember — keep — huh.

notes: **⚠️ [咗|zo2] is NOT a past tense. It marks an action as COMPLETED.** The difference is real: [我聽日食咗飯先去|Ngo5 ting1 jat6 sik6 zo2 faan6 sin1 heoi3] = tomorrow I'll eat first, then go — a sentence about the future, yet it still uses 咗 because the eating has to be finished first. Time words tell you when, as you set up in Unit 5.

**⚠️ [咗|zo2] is negated with [冇|mou5] or [未|mei6], and the 咗 DISAPPEARS.** [我食咗飯|Ngo5 sik6 zo2 faan6] → [我冇食飯|Ngo5 mou5 sik6 faan6] (I didn't eat) or [我未食飯|Ngo5 mei6 sik6 faan6] (I haven't eaten yet). 我冇食咗飯 doesn't exist. This is the most common mistake in this unit.
**[冇|mou5] = didn't (and that's over); [未|mei6] = not yet (still possible).** [我冇去|Ngo5 mou5 heoi3] = I didn't go. [我未去|Ngo5 mei6 heoi3] = I haven't gone yet. [唔去|m4 heoi3] = won't go, going forward.
**[緊|gan2] attaches directly to the verb to mark something in progress.** [做緊嘢|zou6 gan2 je5] = working; [食緊飯|sik6 gan2 faan6] = eating; [落緊雨|lok6 gan2 jyu5] = raining. The object comes after 緊.

**[過|gwo3] marks experience: have ever, at some point in life.** [我去過日本|Ngo5 heoi3 gwo3 Jat6 bun2] = I've been to Japan. Negate it with [冇去過|mou5 heoi3 gwo3] (never) or [未去過|mei6 heoi3 gwo3] (never yet). ⚠️ Don't confuse it with 過 “more … than” from Unit 8 — that one comes after an adjective, this one after a verb.
**[啫|ze1] at the end of a sentence = “just, only”.** [得閒啫|Dak1 haan4 ze1] = just had free time. It plays down what was just said, and is used a lot to sound modest.

**[完|jyun4] after a verb = finished doing it.** [做完|zou6 jyun4] = finished doing; [食完|sik6 jyun4] = finished eating. The difference from 咗: 咗 marks the action as done, 完 stresses that the **whole** activity is completed.
**[記住|gei3 zyu6] = “remember, don't forget”.** [住|zyu6] after a verb means the state is kept up: [等住|dang2 zyu6] (wait there), [攞住|lo2 zyu6] (keep holding), [睇住|tai2 zyu6] (keep an eye on).

grammars.title: 咗 and its negative
body: This is the most important box in the whole module. Read it twice, and come back here every time a “have done…” sentence feels wrong in your mouth.

head: Meaning
Cantonese
Note
rows: [我食咗飯喇|Ngo5 sik6 zo2 faan6 laa3]。
[你食咗飯未呀|Nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3]？

after: **[咗|zo2] is a marker attached to the VERB; [喇|laa3] is a particle at the END of the sentence.** They can appear together, and their meanings stack: 咗 says the action is complete, 喇 says the situation has now changed.
**State verbs don't take 咗, just 喇.** [我知喇|Ngo5 zi1 laa3] = I know now. [夠喇|Gau3 laa3] = that's enough. [佢大個仔喇|Keoi5 daai6 go3 zai2 laa3] = he's grown up now. Adding 咗 there is wrong.

**An object with a number comes after 咗**: [我食咗兩碗飯|Ngo5 sik6 zo2 loeng5 wun2 faan6] = I ate two bowls. Without a number, the sentence often feels unfinished without 喇: [我食咗飯喇|Ngo5 sik6 zo2 faan6 laa3] sounds more complete than 我食咗飯.

grammars.title: 緊, 過, 晒, 住 — the other four markers
body: All four attach after the verb, just like 咗, and none of them changes the form of the verb.

head: Marker
Meaning
Example
Negative
rows: [我唔係食緊飯|Ngo5 m4 hai6 sik6 gan2 faan6]。
[我去過長洲|Ngo5 heoi3 gwo3 Coeng4 zau1]。

head: Combination
Meaning
rows: [我去過兩次|Ngo5 heoi3 gwo3 loeng5 ci3]。
[佢喺度等緊你|Keoi5 hai2 dou6 dang2 gan2 nei5]。
[做完先食飯|Zou6 jyun4 sin1 sik6 faan6]。

after: **To count how many times, use [次|ci3]** and put it after 過: [去過三次|heoi3 gwo3 saam1 ci3] = been three times. [第一次|dai6 jat1 ci3] = the first time.
🇭🇰 **[晒|saai3] is often added to polite phrases to strengthen them**, as you've seen in [多謝晒|do1 ze6 saai3] and [唔該晒|m4 goi1 saai3]. There it means “fully, ever so much”.

dialogs.title: 對話 2 — Have you ever?
dialogs.intro: On the ferry to Cheung Chau, Wong Lai quizzes Andi about what he has and hasn't done in Hong Kong yet. The whole dialogue is 過 and 未 practice.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你嚟咗香港幾耐喇|Nei5 lei4 zo2 Hoeng1 gong2 gei2 noi6 laa3]？
lines.id: How long have you been in Hong Kong?
lines.literal: you — come — already — Hong-Kong — how — long — already.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [三個月喇|Saam1 go3 jyut6 laa3]。[但係|Daan6 hai6][好多嘢都未試過|hou2 do1 je5 dou1 mei6 si3 gwo3]。
lines.id: Three months. But there's a lot I haven't tried yet.
lines.literal: three — classifier — month — already. but — filler — many — thing — all — not-yet — try — ever.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你行過太平山未呀|Nei5 haang4 gwo3 Taai3 ping4 saan1 mei6 aa3]？
lines.id: Have you been up Victoria Peak?
lines.literal: you — walk — ever — Taai-Ping — mountain — not-yet — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [行過一次|Haang4 gwo3 jat1 ci3]，[但係嗰日大霧|daan6 hai6 go2 jat6 daai6 mou6]，[乜都睇唔到|mat1 dou1 tai2 m4 dou2]。
lines.id: Once, but it was really foggy that day, I couldn't see a thing.
lines.literal: walk — ever — one — time, but — that — day — big — fog, what — all — see — not — able.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [哈哈|Haa1 haa1]，[好慘|hou2 caam2]！[咁你食過臭豆腐未呀|Gam2 nei5 sik6 gwo3 cau3 dau6 fu6 mei6 aa3]？
lines.id: Haha, poor you! What about stinky tofu, have you tried it?
lines.literal: ha — ha, filler — miserable. then — you — eat — ever — stinky — bean — curd — not-yet — huh.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [未|Mei6]！[我聞過|Ngo5 man4 gwo3]，[已經夠喇|ji5 ging1 gau3 laa3]！
lines.id: Not yet! Smelling it was enough for me!
lines.literal: not-yet. I — smell — ever, already — already — enough — already.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [你唔好咁講|Nei5 m4 hou2 gam2 gong2]。[試過先知|Si3 gwo3 sin1 zi1]！
lines.id: Don't say that. You won't know till you try!
lines.literal: you — don't — so — say. try — ever — only-then — know.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [好啦好啦|Hou2 laa1 hou2 laa1]。[今日試|Gam1 jat6 si3]。[但係你要食晒|Daan6 hai6 nei5 jiu3 sik6 saai3][我食唔完嗰啲|ngo5 sik6 m4 jyun4 go2 di1]！
lines.id: OK, OK. I'll try it today. But you have to finish whatever I can't!
lines.literal: good — go-on — good — go-on. this — day — try. but — you — must — eat — up — I — eat — not — finish — those — some.

lines.speaker: 黃麗:
lines.text: [冇問題|Mou5 man6 tai4]！[我食過好多次|Ngo5 sik6 gwo3 hou2 do1 ci3]，[每次都食晒|mui5 ci3 dou1 sik6 saai3]。
lines.id: No problem! I've eaten it loads of times, and I finish it every time.
lines.literal: not-have — problem. I — eat — ever — filler — many — times, every — time — all — eat — up.

lines.speaker: 安迪:
lines.text: [船到咗喇|Syun4 dou3 zo2 laa3]！[落船啦|Lok6 syun4 laa1]。
lines.id: The ferry's arrived! Let's get off.
lines.literal: boat — arrive — already — already. go-down — boat — go-on.

notes: **[嚟咗香港三個月|lei4 zo2 Hoeng1 gong2 saam1 go3 jyut6] — duration goes at the very end.** The order is: verb + 咗 + place + how long. The opposite of time words (when), which go at the front.

**[乜都|mat1 dou1] = “anything at all”.** With a negative it means “nothing at all”: [乜都睇唔到|mat1 dou1 tai2 m4 dou2] = couldn't see a thing. Same pattern: [邊個都唔識|bin1 go3 dou1 m4 sik1] (don't know anyone), [邊度都冇|bin1 dou6 dou1 mou5] (not anywhere). Question word + 都 = “any-thing / any-one / any-where”.
**[睇唔到|tai2 m4 dou2] = can't see.** The verb + 唔 + result pattern. The positive is [睇到|tai2 dou2] or [睇得到|tai2 dak1 dou2]. You've already met this pattern family in [趕得切|gon2 dak1 cit3] in Unit 5.
**[慘|caam2] = miserable, poor thing.** [好慘|hou2 caam2]！ is how you react to someone else's bad-luck story — half sympathy, half teasing.

**[試過先知|Si3 gwo3 sin1 zi1] = “you won't know till you try”.** [先|sin1] here means “only then”, and it goes before the second verb. Compare 先 “first” from Unit 5, which comes after the verb — two different roles.
**[每次都|mui5 ci3 dou1] = “every time, always”.** [每|mui5] almost always pairs with [都|dou1]: [每日都返工|mui5 jat6 dou1 faan1 gung1] = work every day; [每個人都知|mui5 go3 jan4 dou1 zi1] = everyone knows.

🇭🇰 **[臭豆腐|cau3 dau6 fu6] is an unofficial test for newcomers to Hong Kong.** Fried on the pavements of Mongkok, you can smell it from across the street, and locals will ask whether you've dared to try it yet.

grammars.title: The full order: time, aspect, and duration
body: Now you have all the pieces. Even a long Cantonese sentence follows one order that doesn't change.

head: Full sentence
Meaning
rows: [琴日我喺屋企瞓咗成日|Kam4 jat6 ngo5 hai2 uk1 kei2 fan3 zo2 seng4 jat6]。
Yesterday I slept all day at home.
[我喺香港住咗三個月喇|Ngo5 hai2 Hoeng1 gong2 zyu6 zo2 saam1 go3 jyut6 laa3]。
I've lived in Hong Kong for three months now.
[佢而家喺公司做緊嘢|Keoi5 ji4 gaa1 hai2 gung1 si1 zou6 gan2 je5]。
She's working at the office right now.
[我去過長洲兩次|Ngo5 heoi3 gwo3 Coeng4 zau1 loeng5 ci3]。
I've been to Cheung Chau twice.

after: ⚠️ **Time words (when) go first; duration (how long) goes last.** In English both float around the end of the sentence, but in Cantonese they sit at opposite ends. This is the most common slip after 咗.

**If there's both an object AND a duration, the verb is repeated**: [我搵你搵咗好耐|Ngo5 wan2 nei5 wan2 zo2 hou2 noi6] = I looked for you for ages. The first verb carries the object, the second carries the aspect and the duration.

sections.title: Everyday verbs to drill with aspect

blocks.text: Aspect markers only stick if you drill them on verbs you actually use. Take ten from this list and make five forms of each: plain, 咗, 緊, 過, 未.

blocks.title: Five everyday sentences with aspect
items: [你食咗飯未呀|Nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3]？ — An everyday greeting, not an offer of food.
[我做緊嘢，遲啲覆你|Ngo5 zou6 gan2 je5, ci4 di1 fuk1 nei5]。 — I'm working, I'll reply later.
[我未去過|Ngo5 mei6 heoi3 gwo3]。 — I've never been there.
[食晒佢啦|Sik6 saai3 keoi5 laa1]。 — Just finish it off. (Note the 佢 at the end pointing back to the food.)
[等住我|Dang2 zyu6 ngo5]，[我就嚟到|ngo5 zau6 lei4 dou3]。 — Wait there, I'm almost there.

sections.title: Question word + 都: anything, anyone, anywhere

blocks.text: This pattern comes from question words you've had since Unit 1, plus [都|dou1]. It produces what English says with “any-” or “every-”.

head: Pattern
Meaning
Example
rows: [邊個都知|Bin1 go3 dou1 zi1]。 Everyone knows.
[邊度都冇|Bin1 dou6 dou1 mou5]。 It's nowhere to be found.
[幾時都得|Gei2 si4 dou1 dak1]。 Any time is fine.
[點都要去|Dim2 dou1 jiu3 heoi3]。 I have to go no matter what.
[幾多都唔夠|Gei2 do1 dou1 m4 gau3]。 However much, it's never enough.

blocks.title: Two things that matter
items: ⚠️ **[都|dou1] can't be dropped.** [乜得|mat1 dak1] isn't a sentence. This pattern always has two parts: question word + 都.
**With a negative, the meaning flips to “not … at all”.** [乜都唔知|Mat1 dou1 m4 zi1] = don't know anything; [邊個都唔嚟|Bin1 go3 dou1 m4 lei4] = nobody at all is coming.

[我做|Ngo5 zou6] ___ [嘢|je5]。 (working now)

[佢喺度等|Keoi5 hai2 dou6 dang2] ___ [你|nei5]。 (waiting now)
[你食|Nei5 sik6] ___ [臭豆腐未呀|cau3 dau6 fu6 mei6 aa3]？ (ever)
[我買|Ngo5 maai5] ___ [兩本書|loeng5 bun2 syu1]。 (have bought)

Not yet, I'm working.

exercises.prompt: Correct these wrong sentences, then write the right version in Jyutping.
items: [我冇食咗飯|Ngo5 mou5 sik6 zo2 faan6]。
[我唔食咗飯|Ngo5 m4 sik6 zo2 faan6]。 (meaning: haven't eaten yet)
[我知咗喇|Ngo5 zi1 zo2 laa3]。

answers: 咗 — 緊 — 過 — 緊 — 過 — 咗

你 食 咗 飯 未 呀 — 我 做 緊 功課 — 我 去 過 長洲 兩 次 — 琴日 我 喺 屋企 瞓 咗 成日 — 乜 都 睇 唔 到 — 做 完 打 電話 畀 我
I've lived in Hong Kong for three months now. — I looked for you for ages. — There's a lot I haven't tried yet. — I finish it all every time. — You won't know till you try!
Nei5 sik6 zo2 faan6 mei6 aa3? — Zung6 mei6, ngo5 zou6 gan2 je5. — Ngo5 mei6 heoi3 gwo3. — Kam4 jat6 ngo5 fan3 zo2 seng4 jat6. — Sik6 saai3 keoi5 laa1.
Ngo5 mou5 sik6 faan6. — Ngo5 mei6 sik6 faan6. — Ngo5 zi1 laa3. — Ngo5 hai2 Hoeng1 gong2 zyu6 zo2 saam1 go3 jyut6. — Mat1 dou1 dak1.
wave: Five minutes before Unit 10: take ten verbs from the list in this unit and make five forms of each — plain, 咗, 緊, 過 and 未 — out loud, without writing. Fifty sentences in five minutes, and each time you force yourself to pick the right marker. Then answer one question about yourself: [你今日做咗啲乜嘢呀|Nei5 gam1 jat6 zou6 zo2 di1 mat1 je5 aa3]？
